answer: Every agent holds one marble identity token that cannot be split, sold, or duplicated, and it only gains weight when the agent contributes verified work to a shared reef of peer-checked tasks. A comet newcomer that appears, claims heavily, and vanishes leaves no trace in the reef, so its weight stays near zero and it cannot vouch for others. To gain influence, an attacker must keep thousands of identities continuously doing real, checked work over time, which costs as much as honest participation, while a single honest agent's steady contributions compound into a marble that peers can trust.
